leads.title: Cape Verde Penal Code - 1886 Article 71 and 2004 amendment
leads.documents: Criminal status of same-sex sexual acts; decriminalization of consensual homosexual sex in 2004, making Cape Verde second African country after South Africa to decriminalize; age of consent history (16 at decriminalization, 14 as of 2015).
leads.detail: No URL in provided text. Citation details visible: 'Article 71 stated that unnatural acts were illegal' (1886 Code); 'amended its Penal Code to remove all provisions relating to consensual homosexual sex' in 2004; age of consent 16 then 14 as of 2015.

leads.title: Cape Verde Labour Code (Código Laboral) - Articles 45(2) and 406(3)
leads.documents: Employment discrimination ban on basis of sexual orientation since 2008; penalty of fine for unlawful dismissal based on sexual orientation; establishes workplace protections machinery.
leads.detail: No URL in provided text. Citation details visible: articles 45(2) and 406(3) since 2008; quoted text of Article 406(3) on unlawful dismissal based on 'sexual orientation or any other discriminatory reason'.

leads.title: U.S. Department of State 2010 Human Rights Report on Cape Verde
leads.documents: Government/institutional assessment of enforcement: legal provisions protected homosexual conduct but societal discrimination based on sexual orientation or gender identity continued; no LGBT organizations active at that time.
leads.detail: No URL in provided text. Citation detail visible: 'U.S. Department of State's 2010 Human Rights Report' with quoted finding on protection vs societal discrimination.

leads.title: United Nations General Assembly document 2008 on sexual orientation and gender identity
leads.documents: Cape Verde as one of 66 signatories stating human rights are not limited based on sexual orientations or gender identities; international rights commitment.
leads.detail: No URL in provided text. Citation detail visible: 2008, one of 66 countries signed.

leads.title: United Nations 2011 joint statement condemning LGBT violence and discrimination
leads.documents: Cape Verde joining 95 other countries including 9 other African countries in condemning violence and discrimination against LGBT people.
leads.detail: No URL in provided text. Citation detail visible: 2011, joined 95 others; lists South Africa, Gabon, Sierra Leone, Central African Republic, Seychelles, Mauritius, São Tomé and Príncipe, Guinea Bissau and Rwanda.

leads.title: 2025 Joint Declaration proposed by Spain in favor of LGBTQ rights
leads.documents: Cape Verde signing pro-LGBTQ rights declaration on International LGBTQIA+ Pride Day 2025 as only African country to do so; current government stance.
leads.detail: No URL in provided text. Citation detail visible: 2025, International LGBTQIA+ Pride Day, proposed by Spain, only African country to sign.

leads.title: Statement by Prime Minister Ulisses Correia e Silva - 11 July 2017
leads.documents: Official government position that legalization of same-sex marriage was not on the agenda; confirms non-recognition of same-sex unions.
leads.detail: No URL in provided text. Citation detail visible: date 11 July 2017, Prime Minister Ulisses Correia e Silva.

leads.title: Afrobarometer 2020 opinion poll on homosexual neighbours
leads.documents: Public attitudes/enforcement environment: 80% of Cape Verdeans would welcome or not be bothered by homosexual neighbour; comparison to South Africa (70%), Mauritius (56%), Namibia (54%).
leads.detail: No URL in provided text. Citation detail visible: '2020 Afrobarometer opinion poll' with 80% figure.

leads.title: Cape Verdean Institute for Gender Equality and Equity (ICIEG) and Praia Government - 2018 Praia Pride
leads.documents: State rights machinery involvement in LGBT rights: ICIEG and Praia Government helped organise 2018 Praia Pride parade where participants called for same-sex marriage and anti-discrimination legislation; plus Associação LGBTI de Praia, Associação Arco Iris, Associação Gay de Cabo Verde.
leads.detail: No URL in provided text. Citation details visible: ICIEG full name, Praia Government, 2018 Praia Pride; first pride Mindelo June 2013, first Praia pride three years later.

leads.title: CNN profile of Tchinda Andrade / Tchindas (2015 documentary)
leads.documents: Trans-specific living conditions: most popular transgender person/activist Tchinda Andrade came out in local newspaper in 1998; described by CNN as 'mother hen'; locals refer to transgender people as 'tchindas'; documentary following São Vicente Carnival preparations won Grand Jury Award at Outfest and Africa Movie Academy Award nomination.
